chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ahmad ibn Hamzah from Aban from Abu Basir who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the child of fornication, does his testimony suffice? He said, 'No.' I said, 'Indeed Al-Hakam claims that it suffices,' so he said, 'O God, do not forgive his sin.'
ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a child born from fornication accepted in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic status of *walad al-zina* (child of fornication) regarding the validity of their testimony (*shahadah*), with Imam al-Sadiq (AS) ruling it invalid. The narration highlights a scholarly debate by referencing Al-Hakam, and the Imam’s invocation of divine forgiveness being withheld underscores the significance of this specific legal ruling in Shia fiqh. It serves as a key precedent for understanding how lineage and moral conduct intersect in evidentiary matters.
